subject: Operator handoff, training, and airlock node maintainability questions
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@stellarnet.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on operator handoff & airlock maintainability

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — StellarNet is very interested in Redwood Private for our analytics cluster that must remain physically isolated. Before we move to procurement, the infra team has a set of operational and contractual questions focused on operator handoff and long-term maintainability of airgapped nodes. Can you confirm the following items or point us to the appropriate docs?

1) Operator training & certification: Do you provide a formal training curriculum for on-prem operators? What is included (slides, lab exercises, pass/fail criteria)?
2) Handoff process for shipped nodes: What does a typical physical handoff look like? Who signs custody, and do you support witnessed handoffs?
3) Hardware maintenance & swap policy: For failed SSDs/NVMe or GPUs on an isolated rack, do you permit workload migration while hardware is repaired? Do you provide replacement hardware or do we procure spares?
4) Credential management & rotation: Can we integrate Redwood Private with our HSM/KMS, and what operational steps are required for key rotation without re-deploying models?
5) Offline patching and rollback: We require the ability to apply OS and runtime patches in an airgapped environment with a documented rollback path — do you have a validated playbook?
6) Evidence for audit: SBOM, signed build manifests, and operator activity logs — can you provide the typical artifacts and retention windows?

If easier, we can take a 30–45 min call with your solutions/ops team. Also, please attach any concise runbook or checklist we can circulate internally.

Thanks,
Anjali Rao
Head of Infrastructure
StellarNet

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on operator handoff & airlock maintainability

Hi Anjali — thanks for the clear list. Short answers here and I attached a very short checklist + training overview to get started. Happy to expand any of these items on a call — would Thursday 6/3 at 10:00 PT work for you and your infra lead?

1) Operator training & certification — Yes. We run a 2-day on-site (or remote, if needed) Operator Bootcamp that includes a slide deck, guided lab (deploy + failover + restore from snapshot), and a short practical assessment. Passing the assessment issues a "Redwood Operator" completion certificate. We can tailor exercises to your hardware model.

2) Handoff process for shipped nodes — Standard is: carrier delivery -> on-site acceptance by customer EHS/security -> vendor (us) performs witnessed boot & firmware attestation before handing over sealed admin key envelope. We support witnessed handoffs and can provide a signed custody form. See Airlock-Handoff-Checklist.xlsx (attached).

3) Hardware maintenance & swap policy — We recommend customer-managed spares for airgapped racks. In practice we support two options: (A) Customer swaps guided by our on-call ops engineer with a maintenance script to preserve KV cache integrity; (B) We send a certified technician under an escorted access agreement. Workload migration is possible if you provision a temporary isolated node pool (we document the steps).

4) Credential management & rotation — Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS/HSM over bring-your-own-KMS connectors (PKCS#11 for HSMs / customer-managed Vault). Key rotation is performed via a key-rotation runbook that updates wrapped keys and refreshes node-level sealed secrets; models are not re-encrypted except for the new wrapping layer. Runbook excerpt in operator-runbook-v1.md.

5) Offline patching and rollback — We maintain an offline patch bundle workflow: signed patch artifacts, prescriptive staging (test pool -> canary node -> fleet), and an automated rollback that uses last-known-good image snapshots. The playbook includes a verification checklist and a staged pause to validate model outputs.

6) Evidence for audit — We can provide SBOMs, signed manifest files, per-operator audit logs with SHA256 transaction IDs, and configurable retention (default 90 days; enterprise can request retention add-ons).

Attaching: Operator-Training-Overview.pdf and Airlock-Handoff-Checklist.xlsx. I've looped Vanessa (ops) to coordinate the technical call.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on operator handoff & airlock maintainability

Anjali — following up with the more detailed artifacts you asked for. See operator-runbook-v1.md (attached) for an excerpt of the rotation and emergency rollback sections. Key points summarized below:

- Witnessed handoff: We support a 3-party signature (carrier, customer security, Redwood engineer). The handoff record includes firmware hashes and a sealed envelope receipt for the admin key.
- Sealed admin key process: Admin keys are issued encrypted and stored in a tamper-evident HSM envelope on first boot; the HSM unseals when the node meets the expected TPM PCR values. We provide the PCR fingerprint in the custody record.
- Disk/GPU failure: We recommend hot-swap where supported. For NVMe swaps we provide a validated swap checklist that keeps the KV cache consistent via a pre-swap mirror snapshot and post-swap cache reconciliation. If hardware is not hot-swappable, we advise using an isolated warm pool to migrate traffic first.
- Offline patching: Patches are delivered as signed .tar.gz bundles transported on a customer-approved media (USB/ODS). The install process is deterministic: verify signature -> stage on canary -> run integrity checks -> promote. Rollback uses the node's immutable snapshot image.
- Operator privileges: We support role-based operator profiles (operator, supervisor, auditor). Only supervisor can initiate key rotations or witnessed handoffs. Operator actions generate signed audit entries (RFC3339 timestamps + operator identifier).

Attachments included: operator-runbook-v1.md, hardware-maintenance-contract.docx. Also adding an SOW training estimate file (SOW-training-estimate.csv) with ballpark numbers for a 2-day on-site engagement + 1 year of optional on-call coverage.

If Thursday 6/3 10:00 PT works, we'll demo the lab and run the 90-min condensed exercise. Otherwise suggest alternate times.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Anjali Rao <anjali@stellarnet.com>

Thanks — that all looks helpful. A couple follow-ups before we lock a date:

• Can you provide sample custody form language for our security team to review (we prefer explicit "witnessed handoff" text including serial numbers and firmware hash).
• For the sealed admin key approach, can you confirm whether the unseal depends on TPM PCRs only (we need to map to our supply chain policy).
• Please include two references of customers who have done a witnessed hardware handoff and airgapped deployment in the last 18 months.
• Finally, provide a short not-to-exceed estimate for the 2-day on-site training + travel + 6-month on-call; we prefer a fixed cap for procurement.

If you can get these by EOD tomorrow we can route to procurement.

-Anjali

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on operator handoff & airlock maintainability

Anjali — appreciate the fast turn. Quick answers and the requested artifacts attached.

• Custody form sample: included in Airlock-Handoff-Checklist.xlsx (tab: Custody Form). Wording includes serial, firmware hashes, carrier seal ID, and signature lines (customer security + Redwood engineer + carrier). We can change phrasing to match your legal team's template.
• TPM PCRs: Unseal is gated by a PCR policy that by default checks PCR0/7/11. We can map to customer-defined PCR values and provide a signed attestation of measured boot. The attestation is stored in the handoff record.
• References: We can introduce you to two customers (contact info redacted for privacy until NDA): "Helix Health" and "PortaEdge" — both completed witnessed handoffs in the past 12 months. If you share an NDA, we'll provide full introductions.
• NTE estimate: See SOW-training-estimate.csv (attached) — 2-day on-site Operator Bootcamp + travel + 6-month priority on-call: USD 38,500 NTE (fixed cap). If StellarNet requires a certified technician onsite for swaps, add USD 12,000 for a year of coverage.

Next steps: If EOD tomorrow is tight, we can provide an NDA template + reference intro by Monday and lock a call for Thursday 6/3.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
